## Today's dataset {.smaller}

336,776 flights that departed New York City airports in 2013.

| Column      | What it contains                                      |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `carrier`   | Airline code — AA = American, UA = United, DL = Delta |
| `origin`    | Departure airport: `JFK`, `LGA` or `EWR`              |
| `dest`      | Destination airport code                              |
| `dep_delay` | Departure delay in minutes (negative = left early)    |
| `arr_delay` | Arrival delay in minutes                              |
| `air_time`  | Time in the air, in minutes                           |
| `distance`  | Distance between airports, in miles                   |
| `month`     | Month number (1 = January … 12 = December)            |

```{r}
#| echo: true
flights |> head(3)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The dplyr toolkit

| Verb                         | Job                                       |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `head()` / `tail()`          | Preview first or last rows                |
| `select()`                   | Keep only the columns you name            |
| `filter()`                   | Keep only the rows that match a condition |
| `arrange()`                  | Sort rows by a column                     |
| `mutate()`                   | Add a new calculated column               |
| `group_by()` + `summarize()` | Collapse groups to one summary row        |

The **pipe** `|>` connects them:

``` r
data |>
  verb_1(...) |>
  verb_2(...) |>
  verb_3(...)
```

## head() and tail()

`head()` shows the first rows. `tail()` shows the last rows.

```{r}
# First 6 rows (default)
flights |> head()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## head() and tail()

```{r}
# Last 3 rows
flights |> tail(3)
```

# 2. select() {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Choose the columns you need**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## select()

The `flights` table has **19 columns**. You rarely need all of them.

```{r}
# Keep only four columns
flights |>
  select(carrier, origin, dest, dep_delay) |>
  head(4)
```

# 3. filter() {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Keep only the rows you want**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## filter()

`filter()` keeps rows where the condition is `TRUE`.

```{r}
# Only flights from JFK
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK") |>
  head(4)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## filter()

```{r}
# Count American Airlines flights
flights |>
  filter(carrier == "AA") |>
  count()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Comparison symbols {.smaller}

| Symbol     | Meaning               | Example                       |
|------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------|
| `==`       | equal to              | `carrier == "AA"`             |
| `!=`       | not equal to          | `origin != "JFK"`             |
| `>`        | greater than          | `dep_delay > 60`              |
| `>=`       | greater than or equal | `dep_delay >= 60`             |
| `<`        | less than             | `dep_delay < 0`               |
| `<=`       | less than or equal    | `arr_delay <= 0`              |
| `%in%`     | is one of a set       | `origin %in% c("JFK", "LGA")` |
| `!is.na()` | has a value           | `!is.na(dep_delay)`           |

::: callout-tip
Use `==` for text or numbers. A single `=` gives an error inside `filter()`. Text goes inside **quotes**. Numbers do not.
:::

# 4. Combining conditions {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Filter by more than one thing at once**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combining conditions

A **comma** between conditions means "and" — both must be `TRUE`.

```{r}
# United Airlines, from Newark, delayed more than 1 hour
flights |>
  filter(carrier == "UA", origin == "EWR", dep_delay > 60) |>
  count()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combining conditions

```{r}
# JFK flights in December that had a departure delay
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK", month == 12, dep_delay > 0) |>
  count()
```

# 5. arrange() {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Sort rows by a column**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## arrange()

`arrange()` sorts rows in **ascending** order by default. Wrap the column in `desc()` to sort descending.

```{r}
# Five most-delayed Delta flights from JFK
flights |>
  filter(carrier == "DL", origin == "JFK") |>
  select(carrier, dest, dep_delay) |>
  arrange(desc(dep_delay)) |>
  head(5)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## arrange()

```{r}
# AA flights to LAX — shortest air time first
flights |>
  filter(carrier == "AA", dest == "LAX") |>
  select(carrier, origin, air_time) |>
  arrange(air_time) |>
  head(5)
```

# 6. mutate() {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Add a calculated column**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## mutate()

`mutate()` adds a column derived from existing columns. The new name goes on the **left** of `=`.

```{r}
# Departure delay in hours
flights |>
  mutate(dep_delay_hours = dep_delay / 60) |>
  select(carrier, dep_delay, dep_delay_hours) |>
  head(4)
```

# 7. group_by() + summarize() {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Compare groups**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## group_by() + summarize()

`group_by()` splits the table into groups. `summarize()` reduces each group to **one summary row**.

```{r}
# Mean departure delay per carrier
flights |>
  group_by(carrier) |>
  summarize(mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE))
```

::: callout-note
`na.rm = TRUE` ignores missing values — cancelled flights have no delay recorded.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## group_by() + summarize()

```{r}
# Number of flights per airport
flights |>
  group_by(origin) |>
  count()
```

# 8. Putting it together {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Chain as many verbs as you need**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Chain everything

```{r}
# Which carrier has the highest mean departure delay?
flights |>
  group_by(carrier) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_dep_delay))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Chain everything

```{r}
# Among JFK flights, which carrier is worst?
flights |>
  filter(origin == "JFK") |>
  group_by(carrier) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean_dep_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_dep_delay))
```

# 9. Summary tables {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Publication-ready tables with gtsummary**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## tbl_summary()

`tbl_summary()` makes a summary table in one step. `by =` gives one column per group.

```{r}
flights |>
  filter(carrier %in% c("AA", "UA", "DL")) |>
  select(carrier, dep_delay, arr_delay) |>
  tbl_summary(
    by = carrier,
    missing = "no",
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1
  )
```

## Recap

| Verb                         | Job              |
|------------------------------|------------------|
| `head()` / `tail()`          | Preview rows     |
| `select()`                   | Keep columns     |
| `filter()`                   | Keep rows        |
| `arrange()`                  | Sort rows        |
| `mutate()`                   | Add columns      |
| `group_by()` + `summarize()` | Summarize groups |

``` r
data |>
  filter(...) |>
  select(...) |>
  mutate(...) |>
  group_by(...) |>
  summarize(...)
```
